findings.explanation: This clause obligates you to perform unspecified and potentially limitless tasks outside the agreed scope simply because you are capable of doing them, risking uncompensated extra work.
findings.suggested_change: Delete this catch-all provision and explicitly state that your services are limited strictly to those detailed in the agreement, with any additional work requiring a separate written amendment and compensation.

findings.quoted_text: The Base Consulting Fee shall be payable in accordance with the Company's normal payroll procedures in effect from time to time.
findings.explanation: As an independent consultant, tying your compensation to internal company payroll procedures creates ambiguity and potential payment delays, as payroll schedules are typically designed for W-2 employees rather than contractors.
findings.suggested_change: Modify the clause to specify that fees will be paid on a fixed schedule upon receipt of your monthly invoice.

findings.quoted_text: The Consultant may voluntarily terminate the Consultant's engagement with the Company at any time by giving the Company 120 days prior written Notice of the termination.
findings.explanation: This imposes an overly burdensome 120-day notice requirement on you for voluntary termination, which is double the 60-day notice required from the Company, restricting your flexibility to leave.
findings.suggested_change: Reduce the Consultant's voluntary termination notice period to 60 days to match the Company's termination notice period.

content.subject: Proposed changes to the agreement
content.body: Hello, Thank you for sharing the agreement. I am looking forward to working together, but I would like to request a few adjustments before signing. - Regarding the relevant clause on unspecified tasks, this creates an obligation for uncompensated extra work outside the agreed scope, so I propose that we delete this catch-all provision and state that services are limited strictly to those detailed in the agreement. - Regarding the relevant clause on payment procedures, tying compensation to internal payroll creates ambiguity and potential payment delays, so I propose modifying the clause to specify that fees will be paid upon receipt of the monthly invoice. - Regarding the relevant clause on voluntary termination, the 120-day notice is overly burdensome and restricts flexibility, so I propose reducing the notice period to 60 days to match the other party's notice. Please let me know if these changes work for you. Best regards,
